title: Standardized protocol for tensile test on palm leaflets
author: Paul Cathelineau

steps.title: Prepare and Dry Leaflets
steps.instruction: Prepare the wet leaflets for drying, ensuring they are clean and properly pressed.

substeps.instruction: Vacuum seal wet leaflets to preserve water content.
If mould develops inside the vacuum-sealed bag, clean leaflets with 70% ethanol using a cloth.
Remove leaflets from the vacuum-sealed bag and ensure all samples are identified.
Place leaflets in a plant press, spacing each layer with newspaper sheets.
Secure the assembly firmly using straps or threaded rods with nuts.
Dry the plant press in an oven at 60°C for 24h.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Measurement
steps.instruction: Cut the samples to size and record physical dimensions and identifiers.

substeps.instruction: Cut leaflet samples using a steel template (100x10 mm) and a scalpel.
Write a unique ID on the samples.
Weight the samples and report the value in the dataset.
Measure three different thickness points using a digital caliper, calculate the mean thickness, and report it in the dataset.
Measure the largest width of the sample over a large area using a digital caliper.
Lightly speckle the samples with a spray of white paint and let them dry.
Using a black pen, mark two points at each longitudinal end of the samples, 25 mm from their center.

steps.title: Tensile Test Setup
steps.instruction: Configure the hardware and software for the tensile test.

substeps.instruction: Optimize camera distance and focus.
Position a lamp to illuminate the test area.
Place the sample between the jaws, ensuring jaws are 60 mm apart.
Run the code from https://github.com/paulcathelineau/CodeMts with the following parameters: Exposure time: 15000 μs, Image width: 800 px, Image height: 3660 px, Frame rate: 5 fps.

Run the tensile bench software to synchronize data (adapting code if not using SyntX software) with the following parameters: Preload: 5N, Load speed: 1mm/min, Rupture detection: delta on Force +/- 5N.

steps.title: Execute Tensile Test and Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform the test, define the region of interest, and classify the rupture.

substeps.instruction: Select the Region of Interest between the two marked points (25mm apart from sample center).
Perform the test and classify the rupture as: 'Jaws' (rupture at the jaws), 'Length' (vertical rupture), or 'Yes' (transversal rupture).
Store remaining leaflet samples in plastic bags for further analyses.

steps.title: Data Processing
steps.instruction: Calculate the Young's modulus using linear regression.

substeps.instruction: Perform a linear regression within the strain range of 0.05% to 0.25% to calculate Young's modulus.
